notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The only tower-specific source is one line in the Forest Lookouts South Carolina index (SAMPIT followed by 'Georgetown County - South Carolina Forestry Commission'). The index is a plain-text dump, so the caption is read as Sampit's by the same name-then-caption layout as SALUDA and SILVERTON. The Silverton per-tower page and its index line ('SILVERTON' then 'Aiken County - South Carolina Forestry Commission') confirm that layout, though no per-tower page for Sampit was found. The Sampit OSM node gave no text, and guessed Forest Lookouts slugs returned 404. Story is about 95 words after the fact-check, under the 120-word floor because the evidence is thin; hold it or pair it with a Georgetown County newspaper source before publishing. The brief's elevation (12 m) is not verified. Search budget used up. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the closure sentence was reworded to avoid copying the quote, and the 'Its tower network' antecedent was fixed.

resolved_conflicts.field: closure date of the fire tower system
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forestry Commission page gives October 1, 1993 as the closure date; the Post and Courier says the last towers closed in 1993 and the system was decommissioned in 1994. The story gives both.
